name: Fascism
summary: Fascism is a family of far-right ultranationalist movements (Italian Fascism, Nazism, Falange, the Romanian Legion, the British Union of Fascists and others) that put the nation above the individual, reject liberal democracy and Marxism, and seek national rebirth under a strong leader and an authoritarian state. The branches share anti-democracy, anti-Marxism, class collaboration in place of class struggle, duties above rights, expansionist nationalism and subordination of property to the nation, but differ on race, religion and economic institutions.
scope: The family of fascist movements, answered only where at least two independent branches state a position and none of the major branches states the opposite. Branches read: Italian Fascism (Mussolini's Doctrine, Rocco), German National Socialism (the 25 points and quoted Nazi writers), the Spanish Falange (26 points), the Romanian Iron Guard (Codreanu) and the British Union of Fascists (Mosley), with Paxton's comparative scholarship. Corporatist institutions in Falange and the BUF are counted as copies of the Italian model, so corporatism is left null. Branch-only positions (Nazi racial doctrine, Italian corporative state) are null or split.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Rocco (Italy) makes property a matter of social utility, German writers treat the owner as a manager answerable to the Volk, and Falange point 10 repudiates capitalism, so the branches subordinate markets to national direction.

public-ownership.rationale: The Nazi programme (13) and Falange (14) call for nationalising trusts, banks and utilities, while Mosley's corporate state leaves industry privately run under state limits.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: The sources opened record no position shared by at least two independent fascist branches on this statement, so no answer is recorded.

unions-good.rationale: The branches reject independent class unions but endorse state-bound ones (Rocco's syndicate as an organ of legal defence, Codreanu's national unions, Mosley's cooperating unions).

property-fundamental.rationale: Rocco says property is a problem of social utility, not of justice, and the Nazi view quoted by Huber says the owner's position is justified only while he serves the community, so property can be overridden.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Nazi programme point 13 demands nationalising trusts, Falange point 13 protects against large-scale finance capital, and Mosley's corporate system disciplines any interest that harms the nation.

cut-welfare.rationale: The Nazi programme (point 15) demands bigger old-age pensions and Falange point 15 keeps and strengthens existing social legislation, so neither branch calls for cutting welfare.
